text:
Please help me write our investor update for the half year. We make sensors that sit inside beehives and tell commercial beekeepers when a colony is weak, so they can treat it before it dies. We're raising a $600,000 bridge round and I want our current investors in it.

Where we are:
- We have 31 paying beekeepers. A year ago we had 12.
- Each sensor costs us $38 to make and we sell it for $55, plus $4 a month per hive for the app.
- Revenue for the last six months was $212,000. 70% of it came in March and April, before pollination season.
- Our biggest customer runs 4,000 hives and lost 18% of his colonies over the winter, against 31% the winter before. He says the sensors were part of it, but he also changed his mite treatment.
- We spend about $95,000 a month and have $340,000 left.
- A large farm equipment company launched a similar sensor in May at $45.

I want the update to say we'll be profitable next year. Keep it under 600 words.

Before I draft, a few questions. Your answers will change what the update says:

1. **What's behind "profitable next year"?** At $95k a month you spend about $1.14M a year, and the last six months brought in $212k, with most of it in March and April. Investors will check this claim first. What does the plan assume: number of beekeepers and hives, cost cuts, a price change, or new channels? If you can't back it with numbers, I'd suggest a weaker but defensible claim, such as "the $600k gets us to X."
2. **What are the bridge terms, and how long does $600k last?** Is it a SAFE or a convertible note? What are the cap, the discount and the minimum check, and is there a close date? $340k plus $600k at your current spend lasts roughly 10 months. Does that get you through next spring's sales season, and what milestone are you raising toward?
3. **How do you answer the $45 competitor?** Your sensor is $55, and theirs costs $7 more than yours costs you to make. Do you have better accuracy, a longer track record, the app, lock-in, or data from customers they don't have? Have any of your customers looked at their product, and did any switch or stay?
4. **What do the 31 customers look like?** How many hives are you in, and how much of the $4/month app revenue keeps coming in? Did any of last year's 12 leave? How much of the revenue is your biggest customer?
5. **Can the 18% vs 31% winter-loss story be stated fairly?** He also changed his mite treatment. Will he let you name him or quote him? Do any other customers have before-and-after numbers?
6. **Who signs it, who gets it, and is there anything investors will learn anyway?** For example a missed target from your last update, a key hire leaving, or a cost that's going up.

1. Fair point, I can't actually back up profitable next year. Use a claim the numbers support instead. One thing I can commit to: we'll bring spending down to $75k a month by February by not filling two open roles.

2. It's a convertible note, 20% discount, $6M cap, closes December 15. One angel has already committed $250k of it. I don't know about a minimum check. Investors who want in should reply to me by December 1. I don't have a specific milestone beyond what you work out from the numbers.

3. Theirs only measures temperature. Ours also measures sound and hive weight. Three of our beekeepers have asked to test theirs. I don't know yet if anyone will switch.

4. I don't know the hive count, the app retention, whether any of last year's 12 left, or exactly how much of the revenue is the big customer.

5. I don't know if he'll let us name him or quote him. I don't know of before-and-after numbers from other customers either.

6. It goes to our current investors, from me at HiveSense. Nothing bad I know of that they'll find out anyway. I can commit to a monthly cash report to everyone who puts money into the bridge.

I've drafted the update below. It's about 530 words, and in place of "profitable next year" it makes a claim the numbers support. Without new revenue, your current cash runs out around March, right when the spring selling window opens. With the bridge, it lasts until about November 2027.

<final_document>
**Subject: HiveSense half-year update and bridge round**

Hi all,

Here's where HiveSense stands at the half year. I'm also asking for something: we're raising a $600,000 bridge round, and I'd like you in it.

**The numbers**

- **Paying beekeepers:** 31, up from 12 a year ago.
- **Revenue, last six months:** $212,000. 70% of it came in March and April, when beekeepers get colonies ready for pollination season. Our revenue is seasonal and will stay that way.
- **Unit economics:** each sensor costs us $38 to make and sells for $55, a $17 margin. Each hive also pays $4 a month for the app, which has no hardware cost.
- **Spending and cash:** about $95,000 a month, with $340,000 in the bank.

**What customers are seeing**

One customer runs 4,000 hives. This past winter they lost 18% of their colonies, against 31% the winter before. They say the sensors were part of that. They also changed their mite treatment, though, so we can't tell you how much of the improvement is ours. We're working to get comparable before-and-after numbers from more customers this winter.

**Competition**

In May a large farm equipment company launched a hive sensor at $45, which is $10 below ours. Theirs measures temperature only. Ours measures temperature, sound and hive weight. Three of our beekeepers have asked to test theirs. I don't know yet whether any of them will switch, and I'll tell you when I do.

**Cutting spending**

We are not filling two open roles. That brings monthly spending down from $95,000 to $75,000 by February.

**Why a bridge, and why now**

Even with that cut, if we count no new revenue, our $340,000 lasts until about March. That's the start of the March–April window that brings in most of our year's sales, and selling more sensors in that window means paying to build them first. Going into our most important season with only weeks of cash is a risk I'm not willing to take.

With the bridge we'd have $940,000. At $75,000 a month, that lasts until about November 2027 before counting any revenue. It carries us through the whole 2027 selling season on cash we already hold.

I'm not going to promise profitability next year. The numbers don't support that yet. The bridge buys us a second full season at lower spending, and in that season you'll see three things: how many beekeepers we add, how many hives stay on the app, and whether we keep customers against a cheaper competitor.

**Terms**

- Convertible note, 20% discount, $6M valuation cap.
- One angel has committed $250,000, which leaves $350,000 open.
- The round closes December 15. If you'd like to take part, please reply to me by **December 1**.
- Everyone who invests in the bridge will get a monthly cash report from me.

I'm happy to answer questions. Reply here or give me a call.

[Your name]
HiveSense
</final_document>

A few things to check before you send it:

- **How I worked out the cash dates:** I counted from today (mid-November) and included no revenue. That's $95k a month through January and $75k a month from February. If the $340k balance is from an earlier date, the dates move.
- **The big customer isn't named.** You don't know yet if he'll allow it. If he agrees to be named or quoted, adding that would make the update stronger than anything else you could add.
- **I left out a few things you don't have yet:** hive count, app retention, whether any of last year's 12 customers left, and how much of your revenue comes from the biggest customer. Investors may ask about them, so it's worth pulling those numbers before the December 1 replies come in.
- **I didn't claim that sound and weight catch more problems than temperature alone.** If you have data showing that, add one sentence about it in the Competition section. It's your best answer to the $45 price.
